checklist.step: Take the reserve rule change into the change queue with a named legal driver
actions: Open the change queue, raise a Normal Change and set Category = Statutory Ledger / Reserves and Regulation = Insurance Business Act Art. 115.
Record the trigger on the ticket: FSA ordinance rate amendment, a new asset class bought by Investment Operations, a chart-of-accounts change, or a close defect.
Ask the Controller for the affected fiscal year and whether the change must land before the 31 March accrual run, and write that into the Required-by field.
Attach the requesting memo and link the ticket to the Japan statutory close release train.
checklist.done: the ticket names the Art. 115 driver, the affected fiscal year and a required-by date ahead of the 31 March accrual.

checklist.step: Confirm the prescribed accrual rates and statutory maximum with the Appointed Actuary
actions: Read the current Ordinance for Enforcement article setting the Art. 115 accrual rates and maximum accumulation limits, and copy each rate onto a parameter sheet.
List the asset classes separately - domestic listed stocks, domestic bonds, foreign-currency denominated assets, foreign stocks, investment real estate.
State for each class the accrual base (book value at fiscal year end) and the maximum limit as a percentage of that base.
Sign and date the parameter sheet and hand it to the Business Systems Analyst as the only authorised source for configuration.
checklist.done: a signed, dated parameter sheet gives one accrual rate, accrual base and maximum limit per asset class with its ordinance cite.

checklist.step: Map every in-scope asset class to subledger security types and GL accounts
actions: Export the Japan entity holdings from the investment book of record with security type, currency, book value and accounting classification as at the last close.
Map each security type to exactly one Art. 115 asset class on the parameter sheet, and mark out-of-scope holdings (loans, deposits, subsidiary shares) with a written reason.
Give the Controller the mapping so each class ties to the statutory ledger account carrying its book value.
Flag any security type with no mapping - an unmapped type silently drops out of the accrual base.
checklist.done: every Japan-entity security type is mapped to an Art. 115 class and GL account, or excluded with a written reason.

checklist.step: Write the configuration specification for accrual, cap and drawdown gate
actions: Draft the spec covering rate table by asset class and effective fiscal year, accrual base source field, posting date of 31 March, reserve account and offsetting expense account.
Specify the cap rule: stop accrual when the accumulated balance reaches the statutory maximum for that class, and never post a negative accrual.
Specify the drawdown gate: a release journal is rejected unless a realized-loss test reference for the fiscal year is attached and exceeds the prescribed threshold.
Specify the timing rule: reserve accounts are closed to posting outside the year-end close window except through an approved drawdown.
Circulate to the Controller, Appointed Actuary and Statutory Reporting Manager for written comment before build starts.
checklist.done: the spec states rate table, accrual base, cap logic, drawdown gate and posting-window lock, and carries all three reviewers' comments.

checklist.step: Configure the accrual rate table in the statutory ledger
actions: In the statutory ledger open the reserve configuration area and create a new rate table version with validity start 1 April of the affected fiscal year.
Enter one row per Art. 115 asset class: class code, accrual rate from the signed parameter sheet, accrual base account, reserve account, expense account.
Restrict the table to the Japan statutory valuation area so the entry cannot reach the IFRS or US GAAP ledgers.
Save the version as Inactive and record the transport number on the ITSM ticket.
checklist.done: an inactive, date-effective rate table version exists with one row per asset class matching the signed parameter sheet.

checklist.step: Configure the statutory maximum cap and stop-accrual behaviour
actions: Enter the maximum accumulation limit per asset class on the same rate table row, with the cap basis set to book value at the posting date.
Configure the accrual routine to post the lesser of (rate x base) and (limit minus current accumulated balance).
Configure a hard error, not a warning, when a posting would carry the balance above the limit, with the message naming the asset class and the limit.
Record the cap values back on the ITSM ticket so the tester can predict the expected stop point.
checklist.done: the cap is configured per asset class and an over-limit accrual is rejected with a class-specific hard error.

checklist.step: Configure the drawdown authorisation control
actions: Restrict the reserve release document type to a posting role held only by the Controller's team and remove it from all standard close roles.
Make the realized-loss test reference a mandatory field on the release journal, sourced from the test produced by the Statutory Reporting Manager.
Route the release to the Appointed Actuary for approval before posting, and block it where the loss test result is below the prescribed threshold.
Check the identity platform to confirm no user holds both the configuration role and the release-posting role.
checklist.done: a release cannot post without a referenced loss test above threshold and an Appointed Actuary approval, and no user holds both config and release rights.

checklist.step: Configure the year-end timing trigger and close-calendar lock
actions: Schedule the accrual routine in the close calendar for the 31 March period, after the investment revaluation job and before the statutory schedule extract.
Set period control so the reserve accounts open only for the year-end close window and close automatically when the Controller signs the close.
Add a dependency so the accrual aborts if the investment subledger feed for the period has not completed, rather than posting on a stale base.
Publish the job sequence to the Statutory Reporting Manager for the business report timetable that ends on 30 June.
checklist.done: the accrual is sequenced after the investment feed, reserve accounts are period-locked, and the job aborts on a missing feed.

checklist.step: Configure content validations on the reserve schedule extract
actions: Configure the Japan business report reserve schedule to pull opening balance, accrual, drawdown and closing balance by Art. 115 asset class straight from the ledger, with no manual override cells.
Add validations: closing equals opening plus accrual minus drawdown; closing is not above the statutory maximum; no asset class present in holdings is missing from the schedule.
Configure the extract to fail and log rather than publish when a validation breaks, routing the failure to the Statutory Reporting Manager.
Attach a sample extract to the ITSM ticket for the Controller to read before release.
checklist.done: the schedule extract is system-fed, carries the three validations and fails closed on a broken validation.

checklist.step: Build and run the UAT scripts against the configured behaviour
actions: Write test cases in the test plan: normal accrual per class, accrual capped at the maximum, negative accrual attempt, drawdown with no loss test, drawdown below threshold, drawdown above threshold with approval, posting outside the close window.
Load a UAT dataset holding at least one position in each Art. 115 class plus one deliberately unmapped security type.
Execute every case, capture posted document numbers or rejection messages, and attach the screenshots to the test run.
Fail the run outright if any negative case posts - a soft warning counts as a fail, not a pass with comment.
checklist.done: every positive and negative case is executed with captured evidence and no negative case posted.

checklist.step: Parallel-run the configured accrual against an independent calculation
actions: Build an independent accrual workbook from the same holdings extract: book value by asset class times the ordinance rate, capped at the statutory maximum.
Compare class by class to the ledger accrual from the UAT run and record the variance in JPY and in percent.
Root-cause every variance above JPY 1 million - mapping gap, wrong rate version, stale base - and re-run after the fix.
Sign the reconciliation and give it to the Controller as release evidence.
checklist.done: the ledger accrual agrees to the independent workbook by asset class within JPY 1 million, with a signed reconciliation.

checklist.step: Obtain Controller and Appointed Actuary approval of the final configuration
actions: Review the configuration spec, rate table export, UAT evidence and parallel-run reconciliation as a single pack.
Confirm the rate table validity dates align to the fiscal year and that no prior-year version was overwritten.
Sign the approval page, then route it to the Appointed Actuary to countersign the rate parameters and the drawdown threshold.
Return any pack missing negative-case evidence rather than approving it with an action item.
checklist.done: one approval page carries the Controller signature and the Appointed Actuary countersignature against the named rate table version.

checklist.step: Take the change through CAB and release it to production
actions: Present the ticket at the Change Advisory Board with the approval page, the UAT run and a back-out plan that reverts to the prior rate table version.
Confirm the release date sits outside the 1 March to 30 April accrual freeze, or attach an explicit Controller waiver if it does not.
Release the transport, activate the rate table version in production, and record the activation timestamp and activating user on the ticket.
Close the ticket only once the production verification evidence is attached.
checklist.done: the change is CAB-approved, released outside the freeze or under a recorded waiver, and the activation timestamp is on the ticket.

checklist.step: Verify the configuration in production before the accrual run
actions: Open the active rate table in production and compare every row field by field to the signed parameter sheet.
Run the accrual in simulation mode against live holdings and compare the simulated amounts to the parallel-run workbook rolled forward.
Attempt one reserve release journal with no loss-test reference and confirm production rejects it.
Record all three checks on the close checklist for the 31 March period.
checklist.done: the production rate table matches the parameter sheet, the simulation reconciles, and production rejected an unsupported release.

checklist.step: File the configuration evidence pack for the retention period
actions: Lodge the parameter sheet, spec, rate table export, UAT evidence, reconciliation, approval page, CAB record and production verification as one pack under Japan Statutory / Art. 115 / FY.
Apply the 10-year retention label counted from fiscal year end so the pack outlives the FSA inspection cycle.
Index the pack by fiscal year, rate table version and change ticket number.
Confirm with the Controller that the pack is retrievable by fiscal year in a single search.
checklist.done: the pack is filed, labelled for 10-year retention and retrievable by fiscal year and rate table version.

testing.step: Build the population of reserve-relevant configuration changes for the fiscal year
actions: Extract every change ticket closed in the fiscal year where the affected component is the statutory ledger reserve area, the rate table, the drawdown workflow or the reserve schedule extract.
Add every configuration audit-log entry touching those objects so changes made without a ticket surface.
Add the 31 March accrual document and every reserve release journal posted in the year.
Reconcile ticket count to configuration audit-log count and clear every difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population reconciles change tickets to the ledger configuration audit log with every difference explained.

testing.step: Reconcile the production rate table to the Appointed Actuary parameter sheet
actions: Export the active and prior rate table versions with validity dates, rates, bases and maximum limits.
Compare row by row to the signed parameter sheet for the same fiscal year and to the ordinance article cited on it.
Confirm each version carries a validity start date and that no closed-year version was edited after that year closed.
List any rate, base or limit difference as an automatic exception with no materiality filter.
testing.done: every active rate row traces to a signed parameter sheet value and no closed-year version was edited.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of changes that altered a rate, a statutory maximum or the drawdown gate.
Take 15 remaining configuration changes selected at random with a recorded seed, plus 100% of reserve release journals.
Record population size, seed, selection date and strata in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
Note any change excluded from sampling and the reason for the exclusion.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all rate and gate changes and all drawdowns, and the seed is recorded.

testing.step: Re-perform the Art. 115 accrual from source holdings
actions: Pull the 31 March holdings extract from the investment book of record independently of Finance, with book value, security type and currency.
Apply the ordinance rate for each Art. 115 class to the book value base and cap at the statutory maximum less the opening balance.
Compare the recomputed accrual to the posted accrual by class and in total and record the variance in JPY.
Confirm every security type in the extract is mapped to a class - unmapped value is a scope leak, not a rounding difference.
testing.done: the recomputed accrual agrees to the posted accrual by asset class within JPY 1 million with no unmapped holdings.

testing.step: Negative-test the drawdown gate in a controlled environment
actions: In the pre-production copy of the current configuration, attempt a reserve release with no realized-loss test reference and capture the rejection.
Attempt a release referencing a loss test below the prescribed threshold and capture the rejection.
Attempt a release above threshold without the Appointed Actuary approval step and confirm it stays in workflow rather than posting.
Report any case that posts as a control failure to the Controller the same day.
testing.done: all three unsupported release attempts were blocked, with the system messages captured in the workpaper.

testing.step: Test segregation of duties over reserve configuration and posting
actions: Extract user lists for the reserve configuration role, the reserve release posting role and the close-calendar administration role.
Intersect the lists and report any user holding more than one, including emergency or firefighter grants used during the year.
For each emergency grant obtain the justifying ticket and confirm the access was revoked inside the stated window.
Report toxic combinations to the Chief Financial Officer, not only to IT.
testing.done: no user holds both configuration and release entitlements, and every emergency grant is ticketed and revoked.

testing.step: Trace each sampled change to its approvals and UAT evidence
actions: For each sampled change open the evidence pack and confirm the Controller signature and Appointed Actuary countersignature both pre-date the production activation timestamp.
Confirm the UAT run includes the negative cases and that none of them posted.
Confirm the parallel-run reconciliation exists and its variance sits inside the JPY 1 million threshold.
Treat a change activated before its approval date as an exception regardless of later ratification.
testing.done: every sampled change has dated approvals preceding activation plus negative-case UAT evidence and a passing reconciliation.

testing.step: Recompute the timing controls against the statutory reporting calendar
actions: Confirm the accrual document posting date is 31 March of the fiscal year and that it ran after the investment revaluation job in the close log.
Test for any reserve posting dated outside the close window to prove the period lock held.
Check the reserve schedule extract was produced in time for the business report submission within three months of year end, on or before 30 June.
Log any out-of-window posting with its document number, user and date.
testing.done: the accrual is correctly dated and sequenced, no out-of-window reserve postings exist, and the schedule met the 30 June timetable.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception carrying the change ticket or document number, the control that failed and the JPY impact on the reserve balance.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list - stale rate version, unmapped security type, gate bypassed, approval out of sequence, feed dependency ignored - and name an owner.
Set a remediation date before the next 31 March accrual and, for any misstated reserve, open a restatement assessment with the Appointed Actuary and the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
Carry every open issue into the following year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a dated remediation and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate over the sampled changes and compare it to the zero-tolerance threshold on rate, cap and gate.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the re-performance variance and the negative-test results.
Have the independent reviewer, who holds no configuration or posting entitlement, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any reserve misstatement to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states an exception rate, a conclusion and the Audit Committee reporting date, and is filed in the repository.

checklist.step: Refresh the legal content behind the curriculum
actions: Re-read Insurance Business Act Art. 117 and the Ordinance for Enforcement articles on outstanding claims reserve and IBNR as they stand at 1 June.
Compare against last year's syllabus and list every change in wording, threshold or reporting basis on a change log.
Add any FSA supervisory guideline update or Local Finance Bureau inspection finding that touches reserve adequacy.
Hand the change log to the Reserving Actuary and the Compliance Manager with an effective date for the new syllabus.
checklist.done: a dated change log lists every Art. 117 text or guideline change since the last curriculum, or states expressly that there were none.

checklist.step: Define the audience by job code from the establishment file
actions: Export the Japan entity establishment file with employee id, job code, cost centre, manager, start date and employment type including contractors.
Select the job codes that touch the reserve - claims handler, claims examiner, claims team leader, reserving analyst, actuarial analyst, statutory reporting analyst.
Add anyone flagged in the claims system as holding case-reserve authority even where the job code is not on the list.
Send the audience list to the Compliance Manager with a named owner per cost centre for chasing completion.
checklist.done: the audience list names every reserve-authorised person with job code, manager and cost centre, sourced from the establishment file.

checklist.step: Build the syllabus around what handlers actually do to the reserve
actions: Write module 1 on what Art. 117 requires: claims payable or likely to become payable but unpaid at year end, including incurred but not reported amounts.
Write module 2 on case reserve setting - when a reserve must be opened at first notification, what evidence supports the estimate, and the prohibition on nil-holding a known liability.
Write module 3 on data completeness for IBNR - accident date versus report date, the reporting lag file, and why late-notified claims must not be back-dated.
Write module 4 on the year-end calendar, the cut-off for claim transactions and the escalation route for a claim discovered after cut-off.
Include three worked Japan examples with numbers and a wrong-answer walkthrough for each.
checklist.done: the syllabus has four modules tied to specific handler actions plus three worked examples with numbers.

checklist.step: Turn the syllabus into a course with a scored assessment
actions: Build course JP-ART117 in the LMS with the four modules, a 45-minute target duration and mandatory module completion before the assessment unlocks.
Write 20 assessment questions - at least 8 scenario questions requiring the learner to decide whether a reserve is required and at what amount.
Set the pass mark at 80%, allow two retakes, and route a third failure to the line manager for coached retraining.
Add a final attestation the learner signs confirming they will open a case reserve at first notification and will not delay reporting past cut-off.
Send the build to the Reserving Actuary and the Compliance Manager for content sign-off before publication.
checklist.done: the course is built with scenario-based questions, an 80% pass mark, a signed attestation and content sign-off recorded.

checklist.step: Sign off the course content before publication
actions: Read the four modules and confirm the reserve basis taught matches the basis used in the year-end Art. 117 valuation.
Check the worked examples produce the same answer the valuation model would produce for the same facts.
Confirm the cut-off dates in module 4 match the published statutory close calendar.
Sign the content approval page and date it before the assignment date.
checklist.done: the content approval page is signed and dated by the Appointed Actuary ahead of assignment, confirming alignment to the valuation basis.

checklist.step: Assign the course and set the completion window
actions: Load the audience list as an LMS assignment group and publish course JP-ART117 with an assignment date of 1 September.
Set the due date 30 calendar days out and configure escalation reminders at day 7, day 21, day 29 to the learner and day 31 to the manager.
Configure an auto-assign rule so any new joiner or transfer into a listed job code is enrolled within one business day of the HRIS record changing.
Confirm with the Compliance Manager that the assignment count matches the audience list count before go-live.
checklist.done: the course is assigned to the full audience with a 30-day due date, escalation reminders and a joiner auto-assign rule live.

checklist.step: Deliver a live session for claims handlers with reserve authority
actions: Run two live sessions covering the three worked examples, with the Reserving Actuary present to answer valuation questions.
Walk through a real anonymised claim from first notification to year-end reserve, showing each screen the handler touches.
Capture the attendance list from the meeting report and load it into the LMS as supplementary evidence, not as a substitute for the assessment.
Log every question the room could not answer and send it to the Reserving Actuary for a written response circulated within five business days.
checklist.done: both sessions ran with the actuary present, attendance is logged and open questions have written answers circulated.

checklist.step: Track completion daily and chase through the line
actions: Pull the completion extract daily from day 7 with employee id, status, score, attempt count and due date.
Send each cost centre manager their open list every Monday, sorted by days remaining.
From day 21, name individuals with reserve authority who remain incomplete in the report to the Chief Claims Officer.
Record every chase - date, channel, recipient - so the escalation trail is evidenced rather than asserted.
checklist.done: a dated chase trail exists for every incomplete learner and reserve-authorised names are escalated from day 21.

checklist.step: Handle deferrals and leavers without leaving a gap
actions: Accept a deferral only for long-term leave, and require a return-to-work completion date recorded on the exception form.
For anyone on deferral, ask the Chief Claims Officer to suspend their case-reserve authority in the claims system until completion.
Remove leavers from the population only where the HRIS termination date pre-dates the assignment date, and keep the evidence of that date.
Sign each deferral personally - no manager-level self-approval.
checklist.done: every deferral has a return date, a suspended reserve authority and a Head of Compliance-level signature, and leaver removals are date-evidenced.

checklist.step: Suspend reserve authority for anyone past day 45
actions: Take the day-45 non-completion list from the Compliance Analyst and match it to case-reserve authority in the claims platform.
Remove the reserve-setting permission for each named user and reassign their open claims to a trained handler.
Confirm the removal back to Compliance with the user id and the timestamp of the permission change.
Restore authority only on receipt of the LMS completion record with a passing score.
checklist.done: no user past day 45 retains case-reserve authority, and every removal and restoration is timestamped.

checklist.step: Test whether the training changed reserve-setting behaviour
actions: Sample 30 claims notified in the two months after training and check a case reserve was opened at first notification rather than at first payment.
Compare the nil-reserve rate at 30 days from notification against the same period before training.
Send handlers with repeat late-reserve behaviour to coached retraining rather than a course retake.
Report the before-and-after measures to the Compliance Manager and the Reserving Actuary.
checklist.done: a before-and-after measure of late and nil case reserves exists and repeat offenders are in coached retraining.

checklist.step: Feed the training outcome into the year-end reserve process
actions: Take the completion register and the QA before-and-after measures into the year-end reserving review.
Where a cost centre shows persistent late notification, widen the reporting-lag assumption for that segment rather than assuming clean data.
Document in the reserve report how training coverage was considered when setting the IBNR assumption.
Raise to the Appointed Actuary any segment where data quality is too weak to rely on.
checklist.done: the year-end reserve documentation records how training coverage and data-quality evidence informed the IBNR assumption.

checklist.step: Report coverage to the Compliance Committee
actions: Prepare a one-page report: audience size, completion percentage, average score, first-time pass rate, open exceptions, suspended authorities.
Compare against the 100% requirement for reserve-authorised staff and the 98% overall threshold.
Table the report at the Compliance Committee and record the minute reference in the evidence pack.
Take any committee action item into the tracker with an owner and a date.
checklist.done: the committee has received completion and score coverage against threshold and the minute reference is in the evidence pack.

checklist.step: Capture the attestations and lock the register
actions: Export the final register with employee id, name, job code, completion date, score, attempts and attestation text version.
Attach the course content version, the actuary sign-off page and the deferral approvals to the same pack.
Lock the register as read-only and record the export timestamp and the exporting user.
Apply the 10-year retention label counted from the training year.
checklist.done: a locked register with scores, attestations, content version and actuary sign-off is filed under a 10-year retention label.

checklist.step: Roll findings into next year's curriculum
actions: Collect the questions most failed in the assessment and the themes from the QA sample of late reserves.
Meet the Reserving Actuary and the Claims Quality Assurance / Training Manager in June to agree content changes for the next cycle.
Add any FSA inspection finding or internal audit exception raised during the year as a mandatory new module topic.
Record the agreed changes on the curriculum change log with an owner and a build date.
checklist.done: next year's curriculum change log names the failed-question themes, QA findings and audit exceptions to be covered, with owners and dates.

testing.step: Build the population from the establishment file, not the LMS
actions: Extract every Japan entity worker active at any point in the training year with job code, start and end dates and employment type including contractors.
Filter to the reserve-relevant job codes and add anyone the claims platform shows as holding case-reserve authority in the year.
Reconcile the resulting count to the LMS assignment count and list every name in one source but not the other.
Treat anyone with reserve authority and no assignment as an automatic exception before any sampling begins.
testing.done: the population is built from HR and claims entitlement data, reconciled to the LMS assignments, with every difference named.

testing.step: Recompute completion rates against the thresholds
actions: Export completion status, score, attempts and completion date for the full population.
Recompute overall completion percentage and completion percentage for reserve-authorised staff separately.
Compare to the 98% overall and 100% reserve-authorised thresholds and record the shortfall in headcount, not only in percent.
Recompute the first-time pass rate and compare it to the figure reported to the Compliance Committee.
testing.done: independently recomputed completion and pass rates are compared to threshold and to the figures reported to the committee.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of deferrals, 100% of learners who needed three or more attempts and 100% of day-45 non-completers.
Take 25 completed learners at random with a recorded seed from the remaining population.
Record the population size, strata, seed and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
State in the workpaper why any name was excluded.
testing.done: the sample covers all deferrals, repeat failures and non-completers plus a reproducible random tranche.

testing.step: Re-perform the completion-date and window calculation
actions: For each sampled learner, recompute the due date as assignment date plus 30 calendar days.
Compare the recorded completion date to the recomputed due date and flag every late completion.
For joiners and transfers, check the assignment date is within one business day of the HRIS effective date.
Flag any completion date that pre-dates the course content approval - it means the learner took the prior year's content.
testing.done: every sampled completion is tested against a recomputed due date and against the content approval date.

testing.step: Re-perform the entitlement suspension for non-completers
actions: Take the day-45 non-completion list and pull each user's case-reserve permission history from the claims platform.
Confirm the permission was removed on or before day 46 and that open claims were reassigned to a trained handler.
Search the claim transaction log for any reserve movement posted by a suspended user after the suspension date.
Treat any post-suspension reserve movement as a control failure reported the same day to the Chief Claims Officer.
testing.done: every day-45 non-completer lost reserve authority on time with no post-suspension reserve movements found.

testing.step: Test the course content against the current Art. 117 text
actions: Open the approved course version taken by the sampled learners and read the Art. 117 module against the statutory text in force during the training year.
Check the worked examples for treatment of incurred-but-not-reported amounts and for the accident-date versus report-date distinction.
Confirm the change log from the June refresh was actually reflected in the published content.
Record a content exception where the taught position differs from the statute, even if completion was 100%.
testing.done: the course content as taken is confirmed against the Art. 117 text in force, with any divergence recorded as a content exception.

testing.step: Trace attestations and evidence for each sampled learner
actions: Pull the attestation record for each sampled learner and check it carries the learner id, the attestation text version and a timestamp.
Confirm the score record and the attestation belong to the same attempt.
For deferrals, confirm the exception form carries a return date and a Head of Compliance signature.
Note any evidence held only in a mailbox or a local file rather than the repository.
testing.done: every sampled learner has a timestamped attestation matched to a scored attempt, held in the evidence repository.

testing.step: Test whether behaviour actually changed on reserve setting
actions: Draw 40 claims notified after the completion window and check whether a case reserve was opened at first notification.
Compute the proportion still at nil reserve 30 days after notification and compare to the pre-training baseline.
Split the result by handler trained versus untrained at the time of notification.
Report any cohort where late reserving is worse after training as an effectiveness finding, separate from the completion finding.
testing.done: a quantified before-and-after comparison of late and nil case reserves is produced and split by trained status.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the learner or cohort, the failed control and whether reserve authority was exposed.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list - audience list incomplete, joiner rule failed, escalation not run, content stale, suspension not applied - and name an owner.
Set a remediation date before the 31 March valuation for anything touching reserve authority.
Carry every open issue into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner and a remediation date ahead of the valuation.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare the recomputed completion rates and the entitlement test results to the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the completion shortfall in headcount and the behaviour measures.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither authored nor assigned the course, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper and the locked register in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states completion rates against threshold, a conclusion and the Audit Committee reporting date.

checklist.step: Sweep every intake channel into the single complaint register
actions: Each morning pull the overnight contact centre dispositions coded as dissatisfaction, the shared complaints mailbox, branch and agency referral forms, and the web form queue.
Open a case in the Japan complaint register for each item with intake date, channel, product, policy number and, where a claim is involved, the claim number.
Pull the designated ADR body's case portal and open a register case for every new referral, recording the ADR reference and the deadline the body has set.
Reject nothing at intake on the grounds that it is 'an enquiry' - reclassification happens at the classification step with a reason recorded.
checklist.done: every channel has been swept for the day and each item exists as a register case with intake date, channel and claim linkage.

checklist.step: Acknowledge the complainant within three business days
actions: Issue the standard acknowledgement naming the case reference, the handler, the expected response date and the right to take the matter to the designated ADR body.
Record the acknowledgement date and the channel used on the case, attaching the outbound letter or email.
Where the complainant is a beneficiary rather than the policyholder, confirm identity before disclosing any claim detail.
Escalate to the Complaints Manager any case where the acknowledgement cannot be issued in three business days, with the blocking reason.
checklist.done: each case carries a dated acknowledgement inside three business days or a recorded, escalated reason.

checklist.step: Classify the complaint against the unpaid or delayed benefit taxonomy
actions: Assign a primary cause code from the fixed taxonomy: claim declined, claim underpaid, claim delayed, benefit not notified to the customer, policy lapsed in error, solicitation or explanation at sale, premium or billing.
Set the Art. 117 flag on any complaint alleging a benefit that is payable or likely payable and has not been paid.
Record the product line, the distribution channel and the branch or agency so themes can be cut by source.
Send the daily list of Art. 117-flagged cases to the Reserving Actuary and the Claims Director / Manager.
checklist.done: every case carries a primary cause code, a product and channel tag, and Art. 117-flagged cases have been sent to Reserving the same day.

checklist.step: Re-look the claim and the reserve on every unpaid-benefit allegation
actions: Open the linked claim and re-read the decision rationale, the policy wording relied on and the evidence on file.
Where the claim was closed nil or closed without payment, check whether a case reserve should still stand because the liability is likely payable.
Re-open the claim and post the case reserve where the re-look shows a probable liability, rather than waiting for the complaint outcome.
Record the re-look conclusion, the reserve movement and the date on the complaint case.
checklist.done: every Art. 117-flagged complaint has a documented claim re-look and, where liability is probable, a posted case reserve.

checklist.step: Investigate and answer the complaint within thirty days
actions: Gather the claim file, the policy documents, call recordings and the solicitation record from the agency where the sale is in issue.
Reach a written outcome - upheld, partly upheld, not upheld - with the reasoning and the wording relied on set out in plain language.
State the redress where upheld: benefit paid, interest for the delay, expenses, and the payment date.
Issue the response by day 30 and record the issue date; where more time is needed, send a holding letter naming the new date and the ADR right.
Attach the outbound response to the case file.
checklist.done: each case has a reasoned written outcome issued by day 30, or a holding letter naming a new date and the ADR right.

checklist.step: Run the designated ADR cases to the body's own deadlines
actions: For each referral from the designated dispute resolution body under Art. 308-2, calendar the body's response deadline on the day the referral lands.
Prepare the company submission with the claim chronology, the decision rationale and every document relied on, cleared by the Complaints Manager.
Attend the mediation and record the outcome, any settlement amount and any undertaking the company gave.
Enter the outcome and any undertaking into the complaint case and into the remediation tracker where a process change was promised.
checklist.done: every ADR case met the body's deadline and its outcome and undertakings are recorded in the register and the tracker.

checklist.step: Pay upheld benefits and interest without a second approval loop
actions: Post the payment for every upheld claim complaint against the reopened claim, with the payment reason coded to complaint redress.
Compute interest for the delay period from the date the benefit became payable to the payment date at the contractual or statutory rate.
Confirm the payment cleared and record the value date on the complaint case.
Notify the Reserving Actuary of any redress payment above the case reserve so the reserve movement is understood at valuation.
checklist.done: every upheld benefit is paid with computed interest, the value date is on the case, and material overruns are notified to Reserving.

checklist.step: Group cases into themes each month
actions: Build the monthly cut of complaint volume by cause code, product, channel, branch and agency, with upheld rate and average days to respond.
Rank themes by upheld volume and by reserve impact rather than by raw count, so a small number of large unpaid benefits is not hidden.
Compare each theme to the prior three months and mark any theme rising two months running.
Open a root cause investigation for every theme above 10 upheld cases in the month or with any single benefit over the escalation threshold.
checklist.done: the monthly theme cut exists with upheld rate and reserve impact, and every qualifying theme has an open root cause investigation.

checklist.step: Run root cause analysis to a named process defect
actions: Take 10 upheld cases from the theme and walk the claim end to end - notification, evidence gathering, decision, communication, payment.
Name the defect precisely: wording ambiguity, evidence request loop, an automated decline rule, a handler authority limit, a broken agency handover.
Quantify the affected population from the claims platform, not from the complaints alone, so silent sufferers are counted.
Write the root cause paper with the defect, the population, the proposed fix and the owner, and give it to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: each theme has a root cause paper naming a specific process defect, a quantified affected population and a proposed fix with an owner.

checklist.step: Sweep the wider book where the root cause bites beyond the complainants
actions: Query the claims platform for all claims decided under the defective rule or wording in the affected period.
Re-decide the sample first, then the full population where the sample confirms the defect, and record each revised outcome.
Give the Reserving Actuary the list of claims requiring reinstated reserves so the Art. 117 outstanding claims reserve captures them at the next valuation.
Contact affected customers proactively rather than waiting for them to complain.
checklist.done: the wider affected population is identified, re-decided, notified, and handed to Reserving for reserve reinstatement.

checklist.step: Fix the process and prove the fix landed
actions: Take the root cause fix into the change queue with a delivery date and an owner - rule change, wording change, script change, authority change or training.
Define the measure that will show the fix worked: complaint volume on that cause code, upheld rate, or days to first payment.
Set the measurement window at three months post-implementation and book the review date.
Close the root cause item only when the measure has moved, not when the change was deployed.
checklist.done: every root cause has a delivered fix, a named measure, a booked three-month review and closure only on a moved measure.

checklist.step: Produce the quarterly complaint statistics for the FSA
actions: Extract the quarter's complaints by category, product and outcome in the format the FSA and the industry association template require.
Reconcile the extract totals to the complaint register and to the ADR body's own case count for the quarter.
Explain every movement over 20% against the prior quarter in the covering note.
Submit within one month of quarter end and file the submission receipt with the pack.
checklist.done: the quarterly statistics reconcile to the register and the ADR count, and were submitted within one month of quarter end with a filed receipt.

checklist.step: Report themes and reserve impact to the Board Risk Committee
actions: Prepare the quarterly paper: volumes and trend, top themes, upheld rate, ADR outcomes, redress paid, reserve impact, open root causes past due.
Name every theme that has been open for more than two quarters and the reason it has not closed.
Table the paper and record the minute reference and any committee direction.
Take every committee direction into the tracker with an owner and a date.
checklist.done: the committee has the quarterly paper with themes, redress and reserve impact, and directions are tracked with owners and dates.

checklist.step: Feed the complaint evidence into the year-end reserve review
actions: Take the year's Art. 117-flagged complaints, reopened claims and sweep populations into the reserving data review.
Test whether reopened claim volumes are already captured in the development data or whether an explicit loading is needed.
Document in the reserve report how complaint-driven reopenings were reflected in the outstanding claims and IBNR reserve.
Raise to the Appointed Actuary any theme where the ultimate exposure cannot yet be quantified.
checklist.done: the reserve report documents how complaint-driven reopenings and sweeps were reflected in the Art. 117 reserve.

checklist.step: Retain the complaint files and keep them retrievable
actions: Move closed complaint files, correspondence, ADR papers and root cause packs into the repository indexed by case reference, policy number and claim number.
Apply the 10-year retention label from closure date, with a legal hold override where litigation is open.
Confirm a case can be retrieved by policy number in one search, since that is how a regulator will ask.
Report any case closed without its response letter attached back to the Complaints Manager for completion.
checklist.done: closed files are indexed by case, policy and claim number under a 10-year label with legal holds applied.

testing.step: Build the complaint population from the channels, not from the register
actions: Extract contact centre interactions in the quarter coded as dissatisfaction or escalation, plus the complaints mailbox, web form queue and branch or agency referral forms.
Pull the designated ADR body's case list for the same quarter directly from its portal.
Match each source item to a register case and list every item with no matching case as a completeness exception.
Reconcile totals and have the Complaints Manager sign the reconciliation before sampling.
testing.done: the population is built from raw channel data and the ADR portal, reconciled to the register with every unlogged item named.

testing.step: Reconcile the quarterly FSA statistics to the register
actions: Take the submitted quarterly statistics pack and the register extract as at the same cut-off.
Reconcile totals by category and by product and explain every difference.
Confirm the submission receipt date is within one month of quarter end.
Flag any category where the submitted count is lower than the register count as a reporting exception.
testing.done: the submitted statistics reconcile category by category to the register and the receipt proves timely submission.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of Art. 117-flagged cases, 100% of ADR cases and 100% of cases where redress exceeded the escalation threshold.
Take 30 remaining cases at random with a recorded seed across channels and products.
Record population size, strata, seed and selection date so the sample is reproducible.
State the reason for excluding any case from the sampling frame.
testing.done: the sample covers all flagged, ADR and high-redress cases plus a reproducible random tranche.

testing.step: Recompute acknowledgement and response deadlines
actions: For each sampled case recompute the acknowledgement due date as intake plus three business days using the Japan holiday calendar.
Recompute the substantive response due date as intake plus 30 days and check the issued response date against it.
Where a holding letter was used, confirm it was issued before the original due date and named a specific new date.
For ADR cases recompute against the deadline the body set, not the internal standard.
testing.done: every sampled case has recomputed acknowledgement, response and ADR deadlines compared to the actual dates.

testing.step: Re-perform the classification independently
actions: Read the complainant's own words on each sampled case and assign a cause code without looking at the recorded code first.
Compare to the recorded code and treat any difference as an exception, including a correct theme with the wrong Art. 117 flag.
Check specifically for unpaid-benefit allegations coded as service or communication complaints, which removes them from the reserve loop.
Record the re-performance note and the evidence read for each case.
testing.done: each sampled case has an independent classification note and every mismatch, including missed Art. 117 flags, is logged.

testing.step: Trace the claim re-look and reserve consequence
actions: For each Art. 117-flagged case, open the linked claim and confirm a documented re-look exists with a date after the complaint intake date.
Where the re-look found probable liability, confirm the case reserve was posted or reinstated and note the amount and date.
Compare the reserve posting date to the next valuation date to confirm it landed in the right reporting period.
Treat an upheld unpaid-benefit complaint with no reserve or payment as a reportable breach, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every flagged case traces to a dated claim re-look and, where liability was probable, to a posted reserve or payment before the valuation.

testing.step: Re-perform the redress and interest calculation
actions: For each upheld case with payment, recompute the benefit due from the policy schedule and the delay interest from the date payable to the value date.
Compare the recomputed amount to the amount actually paid and record the difference.
Check the payment reason code identifies complaint redress so the theme cost can be measured.
Flag any upheld case with no payment and no written explanation of why none was due.
testing.done: every upheld payment is recomputed against the policy schedule and the delay period, with differences recorded.

testing.step: Test whether root causes were quantified and swept
actions: Take the quarter's root cause papers and confirm each names a specific process defect rather than a general theme.
Independently query the claims platform for the affected population size and compare it to the figure in the paper.
Confirm the sweep actually ran, the affected customers were contacted and the list went to Reserving.
Check the three-month effectiveness measure and treat a root cause closed without a moved measure as an exception.
testing.done: each root cause has an independently confirmed affected population, an executed sweep and an effectiveness measure that moved.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with the case reference, the failed control, the customer impact and any reserve consequence.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list - channel not swept, misclassified, deadline missed, re-look skipped, sweep not run, statistics understated - and name an owner.
Set a remediation date inside the next quarter and notify the Appointed Actuary where a reserve consequence exists.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a remediation date and, where relevant, an actuary notification.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the deadline breach rate and the completeness exception count and compare to the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the unlogged complaints and the reserve linkage results.
Have the independent reviewer, who handles no complaints and sits outside Consumer Affairs, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Board Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states breach and completeness rates, a conclusion and the committee reporting date, filed in the repository.

checklist.step: Scope the audit against the statutory notice and disclosure inventory
actions: Take the Japan regulatory obligations inventory and list every notice or disclosure the Insurance Business Act requires the entity to produce in the year.

Split the list into statutory disclosures (explanatory document, business report reserve schedules, price fluctuation reserve balance) and policyholder notices (benefit, lapse warning, renewal, contract change).
For each, record the governing article, the prescribed content and the prescribed timing window.
Agree the scope in writing with the Chief Audit Executive and the Statutory Reporting Manager before fieldwork opens.
checklist.done: the scope lists each notice type with its governing article, prescribed content and timing window, agreed in writing.

checklist.step: Build the population of notices actually issued in the year
actions: Extract the despatch log for the fiscal year with notice type, policy number, trigger event date, generation date, despatch date and channel.
Extract the issued-document archive for the same period and reconcile record counts to the despatch log.
Add the statutory disclosures separately with their publication or submission dates and the location of public inspection.
List every notice type in the scope with a zero count - a notice type that produced nothing all year is a finding, not an empty row.
checklist.done: the population reconciles despatch log to document archive and every scoped notice type shows a count or is raised as zero-production.

checklist.step: Confirm only approved template versions were in production
actions: Export the template library with template id, version, effective date, approver and approval date for every scoped notice.
Compare the template version stamped on issued notices during the year to the approved version effective at that date.
Identify any version used before its approval date or after it was superseded.
Obtain the approval record for each version in use and check the approver was Legal or Compliance, not the producing team.
checklist.done: every template version used in the year is matched to a dated approval by Legal or Compliance covering the period of use.

checklist.step: Draw the sample and record the method
actions: Take 100% of statutory disclosures - the explanatory document, the business report reserve schedules and any reserve-related public statement.
Take 25 policyholder notices per notice type at random with a recorded seed, weighted to types with the shortest statutory windows.
Record population size by type, seed, selection date and the weighting rationale in the workpaper.
Add judgementally any notice produced after a template change during the year.
checklist.done: the sample covers all statutory disclosures, a seeded random tranche per notice type, and every post-template-change notice.

checklist.step: Re-perform the price fluctuation reserve figure disclosed
actions: Take the Art. 115 price fluctuation reserve balance printed in the explanatory document and the business report schedule.
Trace it to the statutory ledger closing balance for the reserve accounts at 31 March, without going through the reporting pack.
Recompute opening plus accrual minus drawdown and confirm it equals the disclosed closing figure.
Confirm the disclosed figure is not above the statutory maximum for the asset classes held, and record the headroom.
checklist.done: the disclosed reserve balance traces to the ledger, reconciles on the roll-forward, and sits inside the statutory maximum.

checklist.step: Re-perform the other reserve figures the notices disclose
actions: Trace the Art. 116 policy reserve and Art. 117 outstanding claims reserve figures in the disclosure to the actuarial valuation output signed by the Appointed Actuary.
Check the version of the valuation output used is the final signed version, not a draft dated earlier in the close.
Confirm the comparative prior-year figures agree to last year's published document.
Record any restated comparative and check the restatement is disclosed rather than silently changed.
checklist.done: every disclosed reserve figure traces to the signed valuation output and comparatives agree to the prior published document.

checklist.step: Test the narrative content against the prescribed content list
actions: Read each sampled notice against the prescribed content list from the scoping step, ticking each required element.
Check required elements are present in substance and not merely cross-referenced to another document the recipient does not hold.
Check the statement of how the price fluctuation reserve was accumulated and whether any drawdown occurred, where the document requires it.
Record a content exception for every missing, ambiguous or contradictory element with the page reference.
checklist.done: each sampled notice is ticked element by element against the prescribed content list with page-referenced exceptions.

checklist.step: Recompute the timing of every sampled notice
actions: For each sampled policyholder notice, recompute the due date as the trigger event date plus the prescribed window using the Japan business day calendar.
Compare the despatch date on the log to the recomputed due date and record the days early or late.
For the explanatory document, confirm it was made available for public inspection within four months of the 31 March year end and record the date evidence.
For the business report, confirm the FSA submission date fell within three months of year end, on or before 30 June.
checklist.done: every sampled notice has a recomputed due date and a measured days-early or days-late figure against it.

checklist.step: Test that despatch actually happened, not just that generation did
actions: For each sampled notice pull the print or email vendor confirmation with the despatch date and the delivery channel.
Check returned mail and email bounce logs for the sampled policies and confirm each was re-issued to a corrected address.
Match the address used to the policy administration address of record at the despatch date, not today's address.
Treat generated-but-not-despatched notices as timing failures, not as production backlog.
checklist.done: each sampled notice has vendor despatch confirmation, a checked bounce status and an address matching the record at despatch.

checklist.step: Walk through the explanatory document build with the producing team
actions: Sit with the Statutory Reporting Manager and walk the document build from ledger extract to published PDF, screen by screen.
Identify every manual intervention - typed figures, pasted tables, edited narrative - and record who performed it and who checked it.
Test one figure end to end through each manual step and confirm the reviewer evidence exists for each.
Record any step where preparer and reviewer are the same person.
checklist.done: the build walkthrough documents every manual intervention with named preparer and reviewer and one figure traced end to end.

checklist.step: Check the public inspection and availability obligation
actions: Confirm the explanatory document was placed at the head office and branch offices for public inspection and record the date it was placed.
Confirm the same document is published on the company's Japan website and retrieve the page with its publication date.
Confirm the prior year's document remained available for the required period rather than being replaced early.
Capture screenshots and site metadata as evidence rather than relying on the producing team's assertion.
checklist.done: public inspection placement and website publication dates are evidenced with captures, including prior-year availability.

checklist.step: Clear findings with the process owners before reporting
actions: Write each finding as condition, criteria with the article cite, cause, effect and recommendation.
Meet the Statutory Reporting Manager, the Policy Admin Ops Lead and the Controller to confirm the facts, not the ratings.
Obtain a management response with a named owner and a remediation date for each finding.
Record any disagreement as a management comment in the report rather than removing the finding.
checklist.done: each finding is fact-cleared with a management response, a named owner and a remediation date, with disagreements recorded.

checklist.step: Rate the findings and issue the report
actions: Rate each finding by regulatory consequence: a misstated public reserve figure rates High regardless of amount.
State the overall opinion on notice content and timing with the sample sizes and exception counts that support it.
Sign and issue the report to the Audit Committee, the Chief Financial Officer and the Head of Compliance by 31 August.
Log every finding in the audit issue tracker with its owner and due date.
checklist.done: a signed, rated report with an overall opinion is issued by 31 August and every finding is tracked with an owner and due date.

checklist.step: Drive correction of any misstated or late notice
actions: For any misstated reserve figure, decide with the Appointed Actuary whether a corrected disclosure or a re-issued document is required, and record the decision and its basis.
For late policyholder notices, direct re-issue to the affected policyholders and quantify any customer detriment.
Notify the Regulatory Reporting Manager where the FSA needs to be told, and agree the wording with General Counsel.
Confirm remediation completion back to Internal Audit with the evidence attached.
checklist.done: every misstatement or late notice has a recorded correction decision, an executed remediation and evidence returned to Audit.

checklist.step: Follow up findings to closure and retain the audit file
actions: Retest each finding at its due date and close only on evidence of the fixed process, not on an assertion of completion.
Report overdue findings to the Audit Committee at each sitting with the days overdue and the owner named.
Lodge the audit programme, population extracts, samples, re-performance papers and signed report in the audit file.
Apply the 10-year retention label from the report date.
checklist.done: each finding is retested and closed on evidence, overdue items are reported to the committee, and the file is retained for 10 years.

testing.step: Rebuild the notice population independently of the audit team
actions: Extract the fiscal year despatch log directly and independently, with notice type, trigger date, generation date and despatch date.
Compare the count and the type breakdown to the population the audit used and list every difference.
Add the statutory disclosures from the regulatory obligations inventory and confirm none were left out of audit scope.
Have the Statutory Reporting Manager confirm the disclosure list is complete for the year.
testing.done: an independently rebuilt population is reconciled to the audit population with every difference explained.

testing.step: Reconcile the disclosed reserve figures to the ledger a second time
actions: Pull the 31 March closing balance for the Art. 115 reserve accounts and the Art. 116 and Art. 117 reserve accounts.
Compare each to the figure published in the explanatory document and the business report schedule.
Recompute the roll-forward and confirm the drawdown line, if any, is supported by a realized-loss test above the prescribed threshold.
Record any difference with its amount and the account it arose on.
testing.done: each published reserve figure is independently reconciled to the ledger closing balance with the roll-forward recomputed.

testing.step: Draw and document a re-performance sample from the audit sample
actions: Take 100% of the statutory disclosures the audit tested and 10 policyholder notices per type from the audit sample.
Add 10 notices the audit did not sample, selected at random with a recorded seed, to test for sampling bias.
Record population, strata, seed and selection date in the workpaper.
State how the unsampled tranche was drawn so it can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the re-performance sample covers audited and unaudited notices with a recorded seed and documented strata.

testing.step: Re-perform the content check against the statutory text
actions: Read each sampled notice against the governing article text as it stood at the issue date, not against the audit's content list.
Confirm the content list itself is complete - a missing required element in the checklist is a worse finding than a missed tick.
Check the price fluctuation reserve narrative describes accumulation and any drawdown consistently with Art. 115.
Record any element required by statute but absent from the audit programme.
testing.done: each sampled notice is checked against the statutory text and any gap in the audit content list itself is recorded.

testing.step: Recompute timing on the unaudited tranche
actions: Recompute the due date for each unaudited sampled notice from the trigger event plus the prescribed window on the Japan business day calendar.
Compare to the despatch date and record days late.
Compare the late rate in the unaudited tranche to the rate the audit reported and test whether the audit sample understated it.
Report a materially higher late rate as a sampling adequacy finding against the audit programme.
testing.done: the unaudited tranche has recomputed timing and its late rate is compared to the audit's reported rate.

testing.step: Verify template approval evidence independently
actions: Export template version history with approver, approval date and effective date for every scoped notice type.
Check each version used in the year has an approval that pre-dates first use and an approver outside the producing team.
Search production output for any notice carrying a template version absent from the library.
Flag versions changed after approval without re-approval.
testing.done: every production template version has a pre-dated independent approval and no unlibraried version appears in output.

testing.step: Verify public inspection and website availability independently
actions: Retrieve the Japan website disclosure page and capture the document, its publication date and the prior-year document still available.
Ask the branch network for photographic or log evidence that the document was placed for public inspection, with the placement date.
Recompute the four-month availability deadline from the 31 March year end and compare it to the earliest evidenced availability date.
Record a finding where availability is evidenced only by internal assertion.
testing.done: availability is independently evidenced by captures and branch records and compared to the recomputed four-month deadline.

testing.step: Test the audit's own evidence and rating discipline
actions: Open the audit file and confirm every reported conclusion has a workpaper reference behind it.
Check each finding has condition, criteria with an article cite, cause, effect and a management response with an owner and date.
Confirm any misstated public reserve figure was rated High and not downgraded through clearance.
Flag findings whose rating was reduced between the draft and the final report without a documented reason.
testing.done: every reported conclusion has a workpaper reference and no rating was reduced without a documented reason.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the notice type or disclosure, the failed attribute and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list - unapproved template, stale content list, manual figure entry, despatch backlog, availability not evidenced - and name an owner.
Set a remediation date before the next explanatory document build and notify the Controller where a figure is affected.
Carry every open issue into next year's audit as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner and a remediation date ahead of the next document build.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare the re-performance results to the zero-tolerance figure threshold and the 2% timing threshold.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing figure reconciliations, timing rates and template approval results.
Have the independent reviewer, who produces no notices and did not run the audit, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee alongside the audit report and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states figure and timing results against threshold, a conclusion and the committee reporting date.
