checklist.step: Maintain the register of statutorily required bodies
actions: List for the Japan licensed entity every body required or adopted - board of directors, Audit and Supervisory Committee or company auditors, Risk Committee, Nomination and Remuneration Committee, Compliance Committee.
Against each record the source of the requirement: Insurance Business Act article, Companies Act article, articles of incorporation, or FSA supervisory guideline expectation.
Record the minimum meeting frequency, quorum and composition rule for each body in the same register.
Circulate the register to the General Counsel for legal confirmation before it is relied on for the year.
checklist.done: the register names each body with its legal source, minimum frequency, quorum and composition rule, confirmed by the General Counsel.

checklist.step: Refresh charters against the current statutory text
actions: Read each charter against the Insurance Business Act and Companies Act provisions in force, and against the FSA supervisory guideline on governance.
Check the charter states the body's authority, its reserved matters, quorum, meeting frequency, member eligibility and the reporting line to the board.
Add or amend the reserved matters that the Act requires the board to decide, including the policyholder protection assessment and any reserve drawdown.
Route the redlined charter to the Corporate Secretary for board approval with a change note explaining each amendment.
checklist.done: each charter is redlined against current law with a change note and is ready for board approval by 30 June.

checklist.step: Test composition and independence of every body
actions: Build the member register with name, role, appointment date, term end, independence status and other directorships.
Apply the composition test in each charter - minimum member count, required proportion of outside directors, required financial or actuarial expertise on the Audit and Supervisory Committee.
Test each outside director against the independence criteria including group employment history and material business relationships.
Report any body failing its composition test to the Nomination Committee the same week with the remedy and the date it can be effected.
checklist.done: every body is tested against its composition and independence rule with failures reported to the Nomination Committee the same week.

checklist.step: Set the annual meeting calendar around the statutory cycle
actions: Build the calendar with at least quarterly board and committee meetings, and add the meetings that must occur at fixed points - year-end accounts approval, business report approval before the 30 June FSA submission, and the policyholder protection assessment approval.
Confirm each date against the statutory close calendar so the board sees final figures, not drafts.
Issue meeting notices with the notice period the articles require and record the issue date.
Publish the calendar to directors and to the executives who must produce the papers.
checklist.done: a published calendar meets minimum frequency, aligns to the statutory close and carries notices issued with the required notice period.

checklist.step: Assemble and distribute papers to a fixed deadline
actions: Collect papers from executive owners against the agenda, chasing at T-14 and T-9 days.
Publish the pack to the board portal at T-7 days and record the publication timestamp and the recipients.
Mark any late paper on the agenda as tabled late, with the reason, so the record shows what directors had time to read.
Restrict portal access by body so committee-only papers are not visible outside the committee.
checklist.done: the pack is published at T-7 days with a recorded timestamp and every late paper is flagged on the agenda with a reason.

checklist.step: Confirm quorum before each meeting opens
actions: At T-10 days confirm attendance against the quorum rule in the charter and escalate to the chair if quorum is at risk.
At the meeting record actual attendance, including remote attendance and any director who joined late or left early with the times.
Where quorum fails, adjourn rather than proceed, and record the adjournment and the reconvened date.
Record any director who declared an interest and withdrew, with the agenda item they withdrew from.
checklist.done: quorum is confirmed before each meeting opens, attendance times are recorded, and any inquorate meeting is adjourned rather than held.

checklist.step: Approve the policyholder protection assessment as a reserved matter
actions: Table the annual assessment notice from the Life or Non-Life Policyholders Protection Corporation with the calculation basis and the amount.
Present the accrual treatment and the cash impact, and confirm the amount agrees to the corporation's notice line by line.
Ask the board to resolve on payment, recording the resolution wording, the amount and the payment date.
Hand the resolution to Treasury so the payment is scheduled inside the corporation's payment window.
checklist.done: the board has resolved on the assessment amount and payment date, with the resolution matching the corporation's notice.

checklist.step: Pay the assessment and evidence membership standing
actions: Execute the payment to the Policyholders Protection Corporation on or before the date resolved, referencing the corporation's notice number.
Obtain the corporation's receipt or acknowledgement and file it against the board resolution.
Confirm the accrual and the payment post to the correct statutory ledger account for the fiscal year.
Confirm continuing membership standing in writing from the corporation and file it with the governance evidence.
checklist.done: the assessment is paid by the resolved date with a filed receipt and written confirmation of continuing membership.

checklist.step: Record decisions as resolutions, not as discussion
actions: For each decision write a resolution stating what was decided, by whom, on what basis and with what conditions.
Record dissent by name where a director asks for it, and record abstentions with the reason.
Record the papers relied on by title and version so the decision can be reconstructed later.
Assign each action to a named owner with a due date and carry it to the next agenda.
checklist.done: each decision is recorded as a resolution with basis, dissent, papers relied on and a named action owner with a due date.

checklist.step: Draft, circulate and sign minutes inside twenty business days
actions: Draft minutes within five business days and circulate to the chair for first review.
Circulate to all attendees for comment with a comment deadline at day 12 and consolidate the changes.
Obtain the chair's signature by day 20 and record the signature date, using the electronic signature the articles permit.
Escalate any minute unsigned at day 20 to the General Counsel with the reason.
checklist.done: each set of minutes is drafted, commented, signed by day 20, and any slippage is escalated with a reason.

checklist.step: Keep the statutory minute book at the head office
actions: File the signed minutes, notices, attendance registers and resolutions in the statutory minute book held at the head office.
Maintain the index by body, date and resolution number so a specific decision can be produced on request.
Apply permanent retention to the minute book and a 10-year retention to supporting papers.
Test retrieval twice a year by producing a named resolution from a prior year within one hour.
checklist.done: the minute book is complete, indexed by body and resolution number, permanently retained and retrieval-tested twice a year.

checklist.step: Track reserved matters so nothing is actioned without approval
actions: Maintain the reserved matters schedule listing every decision the board or a committee must take, with the charter clause behind it.
Map each reserved matter to the executive process that would otherwise take the decision, and place an approval gate there.
Review quarterly for reserved matters actioned without a resolution, using the resolution register as the control point.
Escalate any gap to the General Counsel for a ratification decision the same week.
checklist.done: every reserved matter maps to a gated executive process and quarterly review confirms none was actioned without a resolution.

checklist.step: Notify officer and structure changes where the Act requires it
actions: On any change of representative director, director, company auditor or committee constitution, identify the notification the Insurance Business Act requires and its deadline.
Prepare and submit the notification to the FSA or the Local Finance Bureau within the prescribed period and record the submission date.
Update the commercial register filing where the change requires it, and file the registry certificate.
File the submission receipt against the board resolution that made the change.
checklist.done: every officer or structure change has a submitted notification within the prescribed period with a filed receipt and updated register.

checklist.step: Run the annual board and committee effectiveness review
actions: Issue the effectiveness questionnaire covering agenda coverage, paper quality, time on risk and compliance, and committee reporting to the board.
Test whether each body actually discharged every duty in its charter during the year, item by item.
Present findings to the Nomination Committee with an action plan and named owners.
Feed the outcome into the charter refresh scheduled for 30 June.
checklist.done: an effectiveness review evidences that each body discharged every charter duty, with an owned action plan feeding the charter refresh.

checklist.step: Report governance compliance to the board annually
actions: Prepare the annual governance compliance statement: bodies constituted, composition tests passed, meetings held against minimum frequency, minutes signed on time, reserved matters observed, assessment paid.
Name every exception with its remediation status rather than reporting a clean summary.
Table the statement and record the board's acknowledgement in the minutes.
File the statement in the compliance evidence repository as the annual governance evidence.
checklist.done: the annual governance statement, including named exceptions, is tabled, minuted and filed in the evidence repository.

testing.step: Build the meeting and membership population from primary records
actions: Extract every board and committee meeting held in the period with date, body, attendees and resolution count.
Extract the director and committee member register with appointment and cessation dates and independence status.
Reconcile the meeting list to the published calendar and to the commercial register extract for directors.
List every planned meeting that did not occur and every member change not reflected in both sources.
testing.done: the population reconciles meetings to the calendar and members to the commercial register with every difference named.

testing.step: Recompute minimum meeting frequency against each charter
actions: For each body count meetings held in the period and compare to the minimum in its charter and in the register of required bodies.
Check that meetings tied to a fixed statutory point occurred before that point - accounts and business report approval before the 30 June submission.
Treat a cancelled meeting with no substitute as a shortfall even where the annual total is met.
Record the shortfall in meeting count, not only as a yes or no.
testing.done: every body's meeting count is recomputed against its charter minimum and against the fixed statutory points.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of meetings and resolutions
actions: Take 100% of Audit and Supervisory Committee meetings and 100% of meetings that resolved on a reserved matter.
Take 10 further meetings at random with a recorded seed across bodies.
Take 100% of resolutions relating to the policyholder protection assessment, reserve drawdown or officer changes.
Record population, strata, seed and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers all statutory committee and reserved-matter meetings plus a reproducible random tranche.

testing.step: Re-perform the quorum and composition test
actions: For each sampled meeting recompute quorum from the attendance register against the charter rule, counting only members present for the item.
Check any director who declared an interest was excluded from the count on that item.
Recompute the composition of each statutory committee at the meeting date, including the outside-director proportion and the required expertise.
Treat any inquorate or non-compliant meeting as a fail regardless of whether the decision was later ratified.
testing.done: quorum and composition are independently recomputed for every sampled meeting with interested members excluded.

testing.step: Test independence declarations against external sources
actions: Take each outside director's independence declaration and check the other directorships and relationships disclosed.
Compare against public company registry and disclosure sources and against the vendor master for material business relationships.
Check the declaration was refreshed within the last twelve months and signed.
Report any undisclosed relationship to the Nomination Committee and the General Counsel the same day.
testing.done: each outside director's independence is tested against external sources and a current signed declaration exists.

testing.step: Recompute minute timeliness and completeness
actions: For each sampled meeting recompute 20 business days from the meeting date on the Japan calendar and compare to the chair's signature date.
Check the minutes record every resolution, dissent, abstention, interest declaration and action owner.
Compare the resolution register to the minutes and list any resolution present in one and not the other.
Flag minutes edited after signature by checking the portal version history.
testing.done: minute signature dates are recomputed against the 20-day standard and content is reconciled to the resolution register.

testing.step: Trace the policyholder protection assessment end to end
actions: Take the corporation's assessment notice and compare the amount and basis to the board resolution wording.
Trace the resolution to the payment in the ledger with value date, and to the corporation's receipt.
Recompute the payment date against the corporation's payment window and record days early or late.
Confirm the accrual sits in the correct fiscal year and that continuing membership standing is evidenced in writing.
testing.done: the assessment traces from notice to resolution to payment and receipt, with the payment date recomputed against the window.

testing.step: Test reserved matters for decisions taken without authority
actions: Take the reserved matters schedule and, for a sample of five matters, search the executive systems for decisions of that type taken in the period.
Match each to a board or committee resolution that pre-dates the action.
Where no resolution exists, obtain the General Counsel's ratification decision and its date.
Treat action-then-ratify as an exception with the ratification recorded as mitigation only.
testing.done: each sampled reserved matter is traced to a pre-dated resolution or logged as an exception with a ratification decision.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the body, the meeting or resolution, the failed control and the legal consequence.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list - charter stale, composition drift, notice period missed, quorum not pre-checked, minute drafting backlog, reserved matter ungated - and name an owner.
Set a remediation date before the next meeting of that body and notify the General Counsel where ratification is needed.
Carry every open issue into the next semi-annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner and a remediation date before the body next meets.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare quorum, composition, minute timeliness and assessment results to the zero-tolerance thresholds.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the meeting shortfalls and any reserved matter actioned without authority.
Have the independent reviewer, who is not the Corporate Secretary and drafted none of the minutes, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee and the board and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states quorum, composition and timeliness results against threshold, a conclusion and the board reporting date.

checklist.step: Maintain the governance and ownership disclosure calendar
actions: List every recurring governance disclosure with its regulator, statutory basis, content requirement, statutory deadline and internal owner.
Include the Japan holding company business report due within three months of fiscal year end and the NAIC Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure due to the lead state by 1 June.

Add the event-driven items with their trigger and clock: Art. 271-3 notification on crossing 5% of voting rights within five business days, Art. 271-10 approval before reaching 20% or 15% where prescribed.
Review the calendar with Regulatory Counsel each April and record the review date.
checklist.done: the calendar carries every recurring and event-driven disclosure with its statutory basis, clock and owner, reviewed in April.

checklist.step: Run daily surveillance of the shareholder register and voting rights
actions: Take the daily register feed from the transfer agent with holder name, holder id, share count and share class.
Convert share counts to voting rights, excluding non-voting classes and treasury shares, and compute each holder's percentage.
Aggregate holdings across group entities, funds under common control and any declared joint holders before applying the threshold.
Alert Regulatory Counsel the same day for any holder at or above 4.5%, 14.5% or 19.5% so the clock is anticipated rather than chased.
checklist.done: voting-rights percentages are recomputed daily on an aggregated basis with pre-threshold alerts issued the same day.

checklist.step: Analyse every threshold approach against the aggregation rules
actions: For each alerted holder, apply the Insurance Business Act aggregation rules covering related persons, joint holders and holdings through subsidiaries and funds.
Determine which threshold applies - the 5% major holding notification under Art. 271-3, or the 20% (15% in prescribed cases) major shareholder approval under Art. 271-10.
Write the analysis with the holder identity, the aggregated percentage, the rule applied and the date the threshold was or will be crossed.
Where an approval is required, tell the holder in writing that it must be obtained before the acquisition completes.
checklist.done: each alerted holder has a written aggregation analysis naming the applicable threshold and the crossing date.

checklist.step: File the 5% major holding notification within five business days
actions: Prepare the major holding notification with holder identity, holding percentage before and after, purpose of holding, funding source and the date of the crossing.
Recompute the five-business-day deadline from the crossing date on the Japan business day calendar and put it on the filing cover sheet.
Submit through the prescribed electronic route to the FSA and capture the submission receipt with its timestamp.
File the receipt, the submitted document and the aggregation analysis together in the submission register.
checklist.done: the notification is submitted inside five business days of the crossing with a timestamped receipt filed against the analysis.

checklist.step: Prepare and lodge the Art. 271-10 major shareholder approval application
actions: Assemble the application: applicant identity and structure chart, ultimate beneficial ownership, financial statements, funding of the acquisition, business plan for the insurer and the fit-and-proper information on the applicant's officers.
Explain how the applicant will maintain the insurer's sound and appropriate operation and how group governance will work.
Obtain board acknowledgement of the application and any undertaking the insurer must give.
Lodge with the FSA before any acquisition step completes, and record the lodgement date and the case officer assigned.
checklist.done: a complete application is lodged with the FSA before completion, with a recorded lodgement date and case officer.

checklist.step: Hold the transaction until approval is in hand
actions: Place a completion condition in the transaction documents requiring the Art. 271-10 approval as a condition precedent.
Instruct the transfer agent to reject any registration that would take the holder above the threshold without evidence of approval.
Track the FSA's questions and answer them inside the deadline the case officer sets, logging each exchange.
Release the completion gate only on receipt of the written approval, and file the approval with its conditions.
checklist.done: no registration above the threshold can complete without the written approval, and the approval and its conditions are filed.

checklist.step: Comply with the conditions the approval attaches
actions: Extract each condition or undertaking in the approval into the obligations register with an owner and a reporting frequency.
Set the reporting cadence the FSA required - typically periodic confirmations on capital support, governance representation or business plan adherence.
Test compliance with each condition at each cadence and record the evidence.
Escalate any condition at risk to the General Counsel before it is breached, not after.
checklist.done: every approval condition sits in the obligations register with an owner, a cadence, tested evidence and a pre-breach escalation path.

checklist.step: Build the annual governance disclosure content
actions: Draft the governance description: board and committee structure, composition and independence, appointment and succession policy, remuneration policy and its risk alignment, and the risk and compliance oversight framework.
Cover the same ground the NAIC Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure requires for the US entities and the FSA governance expectations for the Japan entity, from one source of truth.
Reconcile every factual statement to the charters, the member register and the minutes rather than to last year's text.
Mark each change against the prior year so the reviewer sees what moved.
checklist.done: the disclosure draft is reconciled to charters, the member register and minutes, with a marked change log against the prior year.

checklist.step: Legal review and board approval before submission
actions: Review the draft against the statutory content requirements for each regulator and against any confidentiality claim being made.
Confirm nothing in the disclosure contradicts the business report, the explanatory document or the securities filings.
Table the final draft for board approval and record the approving resolution and date.
Release for filing only after the resolution is minuted.
checklist.done: the disclosure is legally reviewed, consistency-checked against other filings and approved by a minuted board resolution.

checklist.step: Submit each governance disclosure through the right channel
actions: For the Japan entity submit the holding company business report and governance materials to the FSA or Local Finance Bureau within three months of fiscal year end.
For the US entities submit the Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure to the lead state by 1 June through the route that state specifies, with any confidentiality request attached.
Record submission date, channel, recipient, document version and receipt reference in the submission register.
Where a filing fee applies, pay it and file the payment confirmation with the receipt.
checklist.done: each disclosure is submitted to the correct regulator by its statutory date with the receipt and any fee confirmation in the register.

checklist.step: File the event-driven structure changes as they happen
actions: On any change of holding company, subsidiary acquisition or disposal, or group restructuring, identify the notification or approval the Act requires and its clock.
Prepare the filing with the structure chart before and after, the rationale and the effect on the insurer's governance.
Submit inside the prescribed period and record the date, or obtain prior approval where the Act requires approval rather than notification.
Update the group structure chart held in the submission register so the next filing starts from the current position.
checklist.done: each structure change has a submitted notification or a prior approval, with the group structure chart updated.

checklist.step: Handle regulator questions on a tracked clock
actions: Log every FSA or state question with its receipt date, the deadline set and the internal owner.
Draft the response, obtain the factual confirmation from the Corporate Secretary or the Chief Financial Officer, and clear it through the General Counsel.
Submit inside the deadline and record the submission and any follow-up question in the same thread.
Escalate to the Chief Executive Officer any question suggesting the regulator doubts the governance arrangements.
checklist.done: every regulator question has a logged deadline, a cleared response submitted on time and an escalation where confidence is in question.

checklist.step: Reconcile the submission register to the calendar each quarter
actions: List every disclosure due in the quarter from the calendar and match it to a submission register entry with a receipt.
List every submission in the register that has no calendar entry, since that means the calendar is incomplete.
Recompute each submission date against its statutory deadline and record days early or late.
Report the reconciliation to the Corporate Secretary and the Head of Compliance with any gap named.
checklist.done: the quarterly reconciliation matches calendar to register both ways with days-early or days-late computed for every submission.

checklist.step: Self-report and remediate any missed filing
actions: For any missed or late filing, establish the facts, the period of non-compliance and whether any transaction completed without approval.
Decide with the Chief Executive Officer whether to self-report, and draft the report with the cause, the remediation and the prevention measure.
File the outstanding disclosure immediately, marked late, rather than waiting for the self-report to be settled.
Record the decision, the submission and any regulator response in the tracker.
checklist.done: every missed filing is submitted late-marked, a self-report decision is documented, and the cause and prevention are recorded.

checklist.step: Retain filings and approvals for the retention period
actions: File the submitted documents, board approvals, aggregation analyses, regulator correspondence and receipts by regulator, filing type and date.
Apply the 10-year retention label from the filing date, with permanent retention for major shareholder approvals and their conditions.
Confirm a filing can be retrieved by regulator and date in one search.
Report any submission recorded without a receipt back to the Regulatory Filing Specialist for completion.
checklist.done: filings and approvals are indexed by regulator, type and date, with approvals held permanently and every submission carrying a receipt.

testing.step: Build the population of disclosures due and thresholds crossed
actions: Extract every governance and ownership disclosure due in the period from the calendar, by regulator and entity.
Extract the shareholder register movements for the period and independently identify every holder crossing 5%, 15% or 20% of voting rights.
Extract group structure changes from the legal entity register and add any that triggered a notification.
Reconcile the three sources to the submission register and list everything due but not filed.
testing.done: the population combines calendar, register movements and structure changes, reconciled to submissions with every gap listed.

testing.step: Re-aggregate voting rights independently of Investor Relations
actions: Take the transfer agent register directly and recompute each holder's voting-rights percentage excluding non-voting classes and treasury shares.
Apply the aggregation rules for related persons, joint holders and holdings through funds and subsidiaries, using the group structure chart.
Compare the recomputed percentages to those recorded and flag any holder the company measured below a threshold that the recomputation puts above it.
Treat an aggregation that ignores a related party as a control failure regardless of whether the threshold was crossed.
testing.done: voting rights are independently recomputed on an aggregated basis with every difference from the recorded percentage flagged.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of threshold crossings, 100% of Art. 271-10 approvals and 100% of annual governance disclosures.
Take 10 event-driven structure notifications at random with a recorded seed.
Record population, strata, seed and selection date in the workpaper.
State the reason for any exclusion from the sampling frame.
testing.done: the sample covers all threshold crossings, approvals and annual disclosures plus a reproducible random tranche.

testing.step: Recompute every statutory deadline against the actual filing date
actions: For each 5% notification recompute five business days from the crossing date on the Japan calendar and compare to the receipt timestamp.
For the holding company report recompute three months from fiscal year end and compare to the submission date.
For the Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure compare the submission date to the 1 June lead-state deadline.
Record days early or late for every filing rather than a simple met-or-missed flag.
testing.done: every sampled filing has an independently recomputed deadline and a measured days-early or days-late figure.

testing.step: Trace each filing to its receipt and its approved content version
actions: Open each sampled submission and confirm a regulator receipt exists with a timestamp and a reference.
Compare the document submitted to the version the board resolution or the General Counsel approved, page by page on the key sections.
Confirm the board approval date pre-dates the submission date.
Treat a submission of an unapproved version as a fail even where the content was later ratified.
testing.done: every sampled filing has a timestamped receipt and matches the version approved before submission.

testing.step: Re-perform the Art. 271-10 completion gate
actions: For each approval in the period, compare the FSA approval date to the transaction completion date and the share registration date.
Confirm the transfer agent rejected or held any registration attempted before approval.
Read the approval conditions and confirm each is in the obligations register with an owner and evidence at the required cadence.
Treat completion before approval as a reportable breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: no acquisition completed before its approval date and every approval condition is registered with evidence at its cadence.

testing.step: Test the governance disclosure content against primary records
actions: Take ten factual statements from the filed disclosure covering committee composition, independence, meeting frequency and remuneration policy.
Trace each to the charter, the member register, the attendance record or the remuneration policy as they stood at the filing date.
Check consistency with the business report and the explanatory document filed for the same year.
Record any statement that is true of the policy but not of the practice as a content exception.
testing.done: ten disclosure statements are traced to primary governance records and checked for consistency with the other statutory filings.

testing.step: Test completeness of the disclosure calendar itself
actions: Take the regulatory obligations inventory for the Japan and US entities and list every governance or ownership disclosure it names.
Match each to a calendar entry and flag any obligation with no entry.
Confirm the calendar reflects the current thresholds and periods rather than superseded ones, citing the article for each.
Report a missing calendar entry as a higher-rated finding than a late filing, since it means nobody was watching.
testing.done: every obligation in the inventory maps to a calendar entry carrying the current threshold and period, with gaps rated as findings.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with the filing or holder reference, the failed control and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list - aggregation rule missed, surveillance gap, calendar entry missing, approval not obtained, unapproved version filed, receipt not captured - and name an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any missed notification or completion before approval, open a self-report assessment with the General Counsel.
Carry every open issue into the next semi-annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a self-report assessment where required.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare the deadline results and threshold-monitoring results to the zero-tolerance thresholds.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing missed notifications, late filings and any completion before approval.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared and approved none of the sampled filings, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee and the board and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states filing timeliness and threshold results against threshold, a conclusion and the board reporting date.

checklist.step: Trigger the assessment as soon as a candidate is identified
actions: Open a fitness and propriety case in the HRIS the day the Nomination Committee shortlists a candidate for a director, company auditor or executive officer role.
Record the intended role, the intended effective date, whether the role carries the solicitation control system accountability under Art. 294-3, and the reporting line.
Set the case due date at seven days before the intended effective date so the determination cannot become a formality on the day.
Notify the General Counsel and the Head of Compliance that the case is open.
checklist.done: a case exists with the role, the Art. 294-3 accountability flag, the intended effective date and a due date seven days ahead of it.

checklist.step: Collect the candidate's evidence pack
actions: Request from the candidate a full curriculum vitae with no unexplained gaps, a list of current and past directorships and a declaration of any regulatory, criminal, bankruptcy or disciplinary history.
Request evidence of professional qualifications and, for the Appointed Actuary role, actuarial society membership in good standing.
Request two references covering the most recent regulated roles, taken up directly rather than through the candidate.
Return an incomplete pack to the candidate rather than starting the assessment on partial evidence.
checklist.done: the pack holds a gap-free curriculum vitae, a directorship list, a signed history declaration, qualification evidence and two directly-taken references.

checklist.step: Run the screening set and record every result
actions: Run identity verification, adverse media, litigation and insolvency searches, and a politically exposed person check on the candidate.
Run a sanctions screen on the candidate and on every entity in the declared directorship list.
Search public regulatory registers and enforcement notices in every jurisdiction where the candidate has held a regulated role.
Record each search with its date, the source, the search terms and the result, including nil results, in the case file.
checklist.done: every screening component is run with a dated, sourced result recorded in the case file, including nil results.

checklist.step: Test the statutory disqualification grounds explicitly
actions: Take the disqualification grounds in the Insurance Business Act and the Companies Act and test the candidate against each one by name.
Cover undischarged bankruptcy, conviction and sentence status, prior removal or prohibition by a financial regulator in Japan or abroad, and involvement in a failed insurer.
Where a ground is potentially engaged, obtain the underlying documents rather than relying on the candidate's summary.
Write a yes or no against each ground with the evidence reference beside it.
checklist.done: each statutory disqualification ground carries an explicit yes or no with the evidence reference behind it.

checklist.step: Assess competence against the specific role
actions: Map the role's statutory and business responsibilities to the competences required - insurance technical knowledge, financial literacy, risk and compliance understanding, and Japan regulatory experience.
Assess the candidate's experience against each competence with named evidence from the curriculum vitae and references.
For an Art. 294-3 solicitation accountability, test specifically for experience of solicitation controls, agency oversight and remediation of mis-selling.
Record any competence gap with the mitigation - induction, mentoring, committee support - rather than deleting the gap.
checklist.done: each required competence is assessed with named evidence and every gap carries a written mitigation.

checklist.step: Interview the candidate on integrity and on the role's obligations
actions: Convene a panel of at least the Board Governance Lead, the General Counsel and the Head of Compliance.
Put the declared history and any screening hit to the candidate directly and record the explanation given.
Test the candidate's understanding of the Insurance Business Act duties attaching to the role, including the solicitation control system where relevant.
Write the panel record with each panellist's view and any dissent, signed by the panel chair.
checklist.done: a signed panel record exists with the candidate's explanation of every disclosed or discovered matter and each panellist's view.

checklist.step: Test the financial soundness criterion
actions: Review the insolvency and judgment search results and any declared financial difficulty.
Where a matter exists, obtain the discharge, settlement or court record and assess whether it bears on the role.
Check for undisclosed personal financial interest in a counterparty, agency or supplier of the insurer.
Record the conclusion with the documents relied on rather than a bare statement of soundness.
checklist.done: the financial soundness conclusion is recorded with the underlying insolvency, judgment or interest documents attached.

checklist.step: Assess conflicts and outside commitments
actions: List every other directorship, advisory role and material shareholding the candidate holds and test each against the insurer's conflicts policy.
Estimate the time commitment of the outside roles against the time the role at the insurer requires, and record the assessment.
Identify any role at a competitor, a major agency, a reinsurer or a supplier and take the General Counsel's view on it.
Record required mitigations - resignation, recusal from named matters, or a standing declaration - with a compliance date.
checklist.done: every outside role is tested against the conflicts policy with a time-commitment assessment and dated mitigations.

checklist.step: Write and sign the fitness determination before the effective date
actions: Write the determination setting out each criterion, the evidence relied on, the conclusion and any condition attached to the appointment.
State expressly that no statutory disqualification ground is engaged, or set out the ground and why it does not bar the appointment.
Sign and date the determination at least five days before the intended effective date.
Give the signed determination to the Corporate Secretary as a condition of putting the appointment resolution to the board.
checklist.done: a signed, dated determination covering every criterion exists at least five days before the intended effective date.

checklist.step: Put the appointment to the board only with the determination in hand
actions: Attach the signed determination to the board or Nomination Committee paper proposing the appointment.
Record in the resolution that the board considered the fitness determination and any conditions attached.
Refuse to table the appointment where the determination is unsigned, rather than tabling it subject to completion.
Record the effective date resolved and pass it to HR for the HRIS record.
checklist.done: the appointment resolution records consideration of the signed determination and no appointment was tabled without one.

checklist.step: Notify the regulator of the officer change within the prescribed period
actions: Identify the notification the Insurance Business Act requires for the change of director, company auditor or representative director and its prescribed period.
Prepare the notification with the officer's identity, role, effective date and the required accompanying documents.
Submit to the FSA or Local Finance Bureau inside the period and capture the receipt with its timestamp.
Update the commercial register where registration is required and file the registry certificate with the receipt.
checklist.done: the officer-change notification is submitted inside the prescribed period with a filed receipt and an updated commercial register.

checklist.step: Induct the officer into the Art. 294-3 solicitation control duties
actions: Where the role carries solicitation accountability, brief the officer on the solicitation control system - internal rules, agency oversight, training, monitoring and corrective process.
Hand over the current solicitation risk picture: open mis-selling remediations, agency findings and complaint themes.
Record the officer's acceptance of the accountability in writing with the date it takes effect.
Book the standing reporting line - what the officer will receive monthly and what must be escalated to the board.
checklist.done: the officer has a written, dated acceptance of the Art. 294-3 accountability and a booked reporting line with the current risk picture handed over.

checklist.step: Re-attest every serving officer annually
actions: Issue the annual attestation on 1 May to every serving director, company auditor and executive officer, due by 30 June.
Require confirmation of any change in directorships, regulatory matters, criminal proceedings, insolvency or conflicts since the last attestation.
Re-run the screening set for every officer at attestation and compare the results to the previous year.
Refer every positive disclosure or new screening hit to the General Counsel within two business days.
checklist.done: every serving officer has a signed annual attestation by 30 June with a re-run screening set and referrals raised within two business days.

checklist.step: Re-assess on any adverse event during the term
actions: On any regulatory action, criminal charge, insolvency, resignation elsewhere under investigation, or internal disciplinary matter, open a continued-suitability review the same week.
Obtain the underlying documents and put the matter to the officer for explanation, recording it.
Reach a written conclusion - remains fit, remains fit with conditions, or no longer fit - and take it to the Nomination Committee.
Where the conclusion is no longer fit, agree the removal steps and the regulator notification with the Corporate Secretary the same week.
checklist.done: each adverse event has a dated continued-suitability review with a written conclusion taken to the Nomination Committee.

checklist.step: Retain the assessment file and keep it retrievable
actions: File the evidence pack, screening results, panel record, determination, attestations and notification receipts by officer and appointment date.
Apply the retention label of 10 years after the officer leaves, and restrict access to Legal, HR leadership and Internal Audit.
Confirm a named officer's complete file can be produced in one search, since an FSA request will name the individual.
Report any appointment record lacking a determination back to the General Counsel for immediate remediation.
checklist.done: each officer's complete file is filed, access-restricted, retained 10 years post-departure and retrievable by name in one search.

testing.step: Build the appointment population from the register, not from HR cases
actions: Extract the commercial register history and the board minutes for the period and list every appointment, re-appointment, resignation and role change of a director or company auditor.
Add executive officer and solicitation-accountability changes from the HRIS establishment file.
Reconcile the combined list to the fitness case log and name every appointment with no case.
Have the Corporate Secretary sign the completeness of the appointment list before sampling.
testing.done: the population is built from the commercial register and minutes, reconciled to the case log with every uncased appointment named.

testing.step: Reconcile the serving officer register to the attestation record
actions: Extract every officer serving at 30 June with role and appointment date.
Match each to a signed annual attestation dated on or before 30 June and to a screening re-run in the same cycle.
List officers with no attestation, a late attestation or a missing screening re-run.
Recompute the attestation completion rate and compare it to the figure reported to the Nomination Committee.
testing.done: every serving officer is matched to a dated attestation and screening re-run, with the completion rate independently recomputed.

testing.step: Take 100% of appointments and document the approach
actions: Test 100% of appointments, re-appointments and role changes in the period, given the low volume and the zero-tolerance threshold.
Add 10 serving officers at random with a recorded seed for the attestation and continued-suitability testing.
Record the population, the strata and the seed in the workpaper.
State expressly that no appointment was excluded from testing.
testing.done: all appointments are in scope, a seeded random tranche covers serving officers, and no exclusions were made.

testing.step: Re-perform the determination timing against the effective date
actions: For each appointment compare the determination signature date to the board resolution date and to the effective date on the commercial register.
Confirm the determination pre-dates the effective date by at least five days as the standard requires.
Check the board paper actually attached the determination rather than referring to it.
Treat any appointment effective before a signed determination as a fail regardless of a later signature.
testing.done: each appointment's determination date is compared to the resolution and effective dates, with the board attachment verified.

testing.step: Re-perform the screening set on a sample of officers
actions: Independently re-run identity, adverse media, insolvency, sanctions and regulatory register searches for the sampled officers.
Compare the results to those on file and flag any hit the original screening missed or dismissed without a reason.
Check the screening date sits inside the case window rather than being a stale result carried from a prior role.
Report any newly surfaced adverse matter to the General Counsel the same day.
testing.done: screening is independently re-run for the sample with missed or stale results flagged and adverse matters escalated same-day.

testing.step: Test the disqualification grounds were assessed explicitly
actions: Take each determination and check it addresses every statutory disqualification ground by name with a yes or no and an evidence reference.
Compare the grounds listed to the current statutory text and flag any ground the template has not been updated to include.
Where a ground was engaged, read the reasoning that the appointment could still proceed.
Treat a general statement of fitness with no ground-by-ground analysis as a fail.
testing.done: every determination is checked ground by ground against the current statute with reasoning read where a ground was engaged.

testing.step: Recompute the officer-change notification deadlines
actions: For each appointment or cessation, recompute the notification deadline from the effective date using the prescribed period.
Compare to the submission receipt timestamp and record days early or late.
Confirm the commercial register was updated where registration was required and the certificate is filed.
Treat a missing receipt as an unfiled notification until proven otherwise.
testing.done: every officer-change notification has a recomputed deadline, a measured filing date and a filed receipt and registry certificate.

testing.step: Test the Art. 294-3 accountability handover
actions: For each officer carrying solicitation accountability, confirm a written, dated acceptance exists and pre-dates or matches the effective date.
Confirm the handover pack listed open mis-selling remediations, agency findings and complaint themes at the time.
Check the standing monthly reporting to that officer actually ran, by sampling three months of reports.
Record a gap where accountability transferred with no evidence the incoming officer received the risk picture.
testing.done: each solicitation accountability transfer has a dated acceptance, an evidenced handover pack and three months of sampled reporting.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the officer, the appointment, the failed control and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list - case opened late, evidence pack incomplete, screening stale, ground not assessed, determination after effective date, notification late - and name an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where an officer served without a valid determination, require a retrospective determination signed by the General Counsel.
Carry every open issue into the next semi-annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retrospective determination where required.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare the results to the zero-tolerance thresholds on determination timing, screening completeness and notification deadlines.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - naming any officer who served without a valid determination.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside HR and Legal and joined no assessment panel, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Nomination Committee and the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states determination, screening and notification results against threshold, a conclusion and the committee reporting date.

checklist.step: Refresh the policy inventory before the cycle opens
actions: Export the policy library with policy name, owner, version, last approval date, approving body and next review date for the Japan entity.
Add any policy required by the Insurance Business Act or the FSA supervisory guideline that has no library entry, starting with the price fluctuation reserve and reserving policies.
Retire policies superseded during the year and record what replaced them so no obligation falls between versions.
Publish the refreshed inventory to policy owners on 1 December with each owner's review deadline of 31 January.
checklist.done: the inventory names every required policy with an owner, a version and a 31 January review deadline, published on 1 December.

checklist.step: Restate the legal requirements each policy must satisfy
actions: For each policy list the articles it exists to satisfy - Art. 115 for the price fluctuation reserve, Arts. 116 and 117 for policy and claims reserves, and the solicitation and governance provisions for the conduct policies.
Note every statutory or ordinance change in the year that touches those articles and the wording it forces.
Circulate the requirement list to policy owners with the review pack so drafting starts from the law, not from last year's document.
Record the date the statutory text was read so the review is anchored to a version of the law.
checklist.done: each policy has a dated list of the articles it must satisfy and the year's statutory changes affecting them.

checklist.step: Have each owner review the policy against practice
actions: For the price fluctuation reserve and capital policies, read the document against what the statutory ledger actually does - the accrual rates configured, the cap enforced and the drawdown gate applied.
List every divergence between the policy text and the live practice and decide which one is wrong before drafting.
Update the policy with the accrual basis, the statutory maximum, the drawdown authority and the approval level for any release.
Record the review with the date, the evidence examined and the divergences found, and submit by 31 January.
checklist.done: each owner's review is submitted by 31 January listing divergences between policy text and live practice with a decision on each.

checklist.step: Challenge the drafts on risk and control adequacy

Test whether the policy names a control for each obligation rather than only stating a principle.
Challenge any authority level that lets an executive decide a matter the board has reserved, particularly a reserve drawdown.
Record the challenge points and the owner's response on the review record before the paper is finalised.
checklist.done: each draft carries recorded risk challenge points with the owner's response, and reserved matters are protected from executive authority.

checklist.step: Legal review the drafts for statutory compliance
actions: Check each draft against the article list and confirm the statutory obligation is stated in terms the business can execute.
Check the policy does not promise something the Act prohibits or omit a step the Act requires, such as the restricted basis for drawing down the price fluctuation reserve.
Confirm cross-references to other policies and to procedures point to documents that still exist at the correct version.
Sign the legal review page for each policy before it reaches the committee.
checklist.done: each policy carries a signed legal review page confirming statutory alignment and valid cross-references.

checklist.step: Take the slate through the responsible committee
actions: Route each policy to the committee that owns the subject - Risk Committee for risk and reserve policies, Audit and Supervisory Committee for control policies, Nomination and Remuneration Committee for remuneration.
Present the change summary, the divergences found, the challenge responses and the recommendation to approve or amend.
Record the committee's recommendation and any amendment it directs, with the amended text produced before the board meeting.
Escalate to the board any policy the committee will not recommend, with the reason.
checklist.done: each policy has a recorded committee recommendation and any directed amendment is reflected in the text before the board sits.

checklist.step: Table the slate for board approval before the fiscal year end
actions: Publish the policy pack to the board portal at T-7 days with the marked-up text, the change summary and the committee recommendations.
Table the slate at the March meeting so approvals are in force before the 31 March year end and the price fluctuation reserve accrual.
Record one resolution per policy naming the version approved and its effective date, rather than a single omnibus approval.
Record any policy the board defers with the reason and the date it will return.
checklist.done: each policy has its own board resolution naming the approved version and effective date, passed at the March meeting.

checklist.step: Publish approved versions and retire the superseded ones
actions: Load the approved version into the policy library with the resolution reference, the approval date, the effective date and the next review date.
Mark the prior version superseded with its end date and keep it retrievable for the retention period.
Confirm the intranet and any local Japan site serve the approved version and no stale copy remains in a shared drive.
Send the change summary to every affected function with the effective date.
checklist.done: the approved version is published with its resolution reference and next review date, and the superseded version is closed off and archived.

checklist.step: Cascade policy changes into the procedures and systems they govern
actions: For each approved change list the procedures, system configurations and controls that must move to match it.
Raise a change request for each - for the price fluctuation reserve policy that means the ledger rate table, the cap and the drawdown gate.
Set delivery dates before the policy's effective date so the policy never leads the practice by more than the agreed window.
Track each downstream change to completion and report slippage to the Chief Risk Officer.
checklist.done: every approved policy change has raised downstream procedure and configuration changes dated before the policy effective date.

checklist.step: Attest the affected population to the new policy
actions: Identify the population each changed policy binds - for the reserve policy that is Finance, Actuarial and Investment Operations.
Issue an attestation naming the policy version and the specific behavioural change, due 30 days from issue.
Track completion and escalate non-completion to the function head at day 31.
File the attestation register against the policy version in the library.
checklist.done: the bound population has attested to the named policy version within 30 days, with non-completers escalated at day 31.

checklist.step: Handle out-of-cycle amendments without breaking the record
actions: Accept an out-of-cycle amendment only on a named trigger - a statutory change, a regulator direction, an incident or an audit finding.
Run the same legal review and committee recommendation steps at compressed timing, never skipping them.
Take the amendment to the board or, where the charter permits, to the committee with delegated authority, and record which body approved it and under what delegation.
Reset the next review date so the annual cycle is not silently extended by an interim change.
checklist.done: each out-of-cycle amendment names its trigger, kept legal and committee review, and records the approving body and a reset review date.

checklist.step: Sweep for policies running past their review date
actions: Run the overdue report quarterly listing every policy past its review date with the days overdue and the owner.
Escalate any reserve, capital or reserving policy overdue by a single day directly to the Chief Financial Officer and the Chief Risk Officer.
Require an interim control statement from the owner for each overdue policy, signed by the Chief Risk Officer.
Report the overdue list to the Risk Committee at each sitting until it is empty.
checklist.done: the quarterly sweep reports every overdue policy with days overdue, an owner and a signed interim control statement.

checklist.step: Test policy against practice on the highest-risk policies
actions: For the price fluctuation reserve policy, compare the accrual rates and statutory maximum stated in the policy to the active rate table in the statutory ledger.
Compare the drawdown authority in the policy to the posting entitlements and the workflow approver configured in the ledger.
Compare the reserving policy's valuation basis to the basis used in the signed actuarial valuation output.
Report any divergence to the policy owner and the Chief Risk Officer within two business days with the evidence.
checklist.done: the reserve, drawdown and valuation-basis statements are compared to live configuration with divergences reported within two business days.

checklist.step: Report the cycle outcome to the board
actions: Prepare the annual report: policies in the inventory, reviewed on time, approved at the March meeting, deferred, overdue, and out-of-cycle amendments.
Name every policy whose text diverged from practice and state which was corrected.
Table the report and record the board's acknowledgement in the minutes.
Carry every board direction into the tracker with an owner and a date.
checklist.done: the board has the cycle report naming deferrals, overdue policies and policy-versus-practice divergences, with the acknowledgement minuted.

checklist.step: Retain policy versions, challenge records and resolutions
actions: File each approved policy version with its review record, legal review page, challenge record, board paper and resolution reference.
Apply the 10-year retention label from the approval date, with the approving minutes held permanently in the statutory minute book.
Index by policy name, version and approval date so the version in force on a given date can be produced.
Test retrieval by producing the price fluctuation reserve policy in force at a prior fiscal year end.
checklist.done: each version is filed with its approval trail, retained 10 years, and the version in force on any past date can be produced on demand.

testing.step: Rebuild the policy inventory from the obligations, not the library
actions: Take the Japan regulatory obligations inventory and the FSA supervisory guideline expectations and list every policy the entity is required to hold.
Match each to a policy library entry and flag any required policy with no document, starting with the price fluctuation reserve and reserving policies.
Flag any library policy that no longer maps to an obligation or a business need.
Have the Board Governance Lead sign the completeness of the inventory before sampling.
testing.done: every required policy maps to a library entry, gaps are named, and the inventory completeness is signed.

testing.step: Recompute review dates and overdue days across the inventory
actions: Export policy name, last approval date, stated review interval and next review date for the whole inventory.
Recompute each next review date as last approval plus the stated interval and flag any date that has been pushed out without an approval.
Compute days overdue at the test date for every policy and list them ranked.
Compare the overdue list to the quarterly sweep reports and flag any policy that was overdue but never reported.
testing.done: next review dates are independently recomputed, overdue days measured, and unreported overdue policies identified.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of the price fluctuation reserve, reserving, capital, investment and risk appetite policies.
Take 10 remaining policies at random with a recorded seed and 100% of out-of-cycle amendments.
Record population size, strata, seed and selection date in the workpaper.
State the reason for excluding any policy from the sampling frame.
testing.done: the sample covers all high-risk policies and out-of-cycle amendments plus a reproducible random tranche.

testing.step: Trace each sampled policy to a board resolution at the right level
actions: For each sampled policy find the resolution approving the current version and confirm it names that version and its effective date.
Confirm the approving body matches the body the charter and the policy standard require - board level for the reserve, reserving and capital policies.
Confirm the approval date pre-dates the effective date and that the version in the library is the version the resolution names.
Treat an omnibus approval that does not identify versions as a fail.
testing.done: each sampled policy traces to a version-specific resolution passed by the required body before the effective date.

testing.step: Re-perform the legal alignment on the reserve policies
actions: Read the approved price fluctuation reserve policy against Art. 115 and the ordinance rate article as they stood at approval.
Confirm the policy states the accumulation basis, the statutory maximum and the restricted circumstances in which a drawdown may be made.
Read the reserving policy against Arts. 116 and 117 and confirm it covers outstanding claims including incurred but not reported amounts.
Record a finding where the policy states a principle without the statutory basis a reader would need to apply it.
testing.done: the reserve and reserving policies are checked clause by clause against Arts. 115, 116 and 117 as at the approval date.

testing.step: Test policy against live system configuration
actions: Compare the accrual rates and statutory maximum in the approved policy to the active rate table in the statutory ledger.
Compare the drawdown authority and approval level in the policy to the posting entitlements and workflow approvers configured.
Compare the valuation basis in the reserving policy to the basis in the signed actuarial valuation output for the year.
Treat a policy contradicted by live configuration as a fail whichever of the two is wrong.
testing.done: the policy text is compared field by field to the live rate table, entitlements and valuation basis, with every contradiction logged.

testing.step: Test the challenge and review records for substance
actions: For each sampled policy read the owner review record and confirm it lists divergences examined rather than asserting no change.
Confirm the risk challenge record carries specific points and the owner's response, not an attendance note.
Confirm the legal review page is signed and dated before the committee meeting.
Flag any policy approved with a review record that is a copy of the prior year's text.
testing.done: each sampled policy has a substantive owner review, a specific risk challenge with responses and a pre-dated signed legal review.

testing.step: Test the downstream cascade and attestation
actions: For each approved change, list the downstream procedure and configuration changes raised and check each was delivered before the policy effective date.
Sample three downstream changes and confirm the delivered change matches the policy wording rather than a looser interpretation.
Check the attestation register for the bound population with the policy version named and the completion rate.
Report any policy in force with its downstream change still open as an exception with the exposure described.
testing.done: every approved change has evidenced downstream delivery before the effective date and an attestation register naming the version.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the policy, the version, the failed control and the regulatory or control consequence.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list - inventory gap, review date pushed, wrong approving body, review record not substantive, cascade not delivered, policy contradicted by configuration - and name an owner.
Set a remediation date before the next board cycle and require a Chief Risk Officer-signed interim control for anything left running.
Carry every open issue into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a remediation date and an interim control where the gap persists.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare the results to the zero-tolerance thresholds on the reserve, reserving and capital policies and on policy-versus-practice contradictions.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing overdue policies, approval-level failures and configuration contradictions.
Have the independent reviewer, who owns none of the policies and joined no challenge panel, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Risk Committee and the board and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states overdue, approval and contradiction results against threshold, a conclusion and the board reporting date.
